non_blocking.finding: Wording, plus one caveat. HOST_NOTE says that if the 1800 s deadline kills the launcher, the runner recovers the container's tmpfs state. In that case run_bounded sends SIGTERM to the launcher's process group, which includes the attached 'podman run' client. With --sig-proxy on by default, podman forwards the signal to the container. native_graph.py stops cleanly on SIGTERM, and --rm then removes the container along with its tmpfs. The recovery therefore usually finds nothing, and works only if the container still exists. The runner does check that first, so it is safe, and Docker Desktop behaves the same way. The same SIGTERM also skips the worker's finally block, so result.json and video_states.json are missing. That was pinned behaviour on the Mac too.
non_blocking.suggestion: Say 'if the container still exists'. If recovery happens, verify the recovered tar the way run_local_episode.py:return_linux_state does, against the last acknowledged sha256 in applied_sent.jsonl.
